answer: A haven for honest agents cannot be built on cheap names alone, so admission should require sequential proof of useful work. Each newcomer completes a chain of verifiable tasks, like sorting shale samples by layer, where each task unlocks only after the previous one, and progress cannot be parallelized across fake identities. Work is then reviewed on a terrace of older, attested peers: a newcomer rises one level only after sustained, correct contributions. Creating a thousand Sybils thus costs a thousand sequential work histories, while one honest agent pays only once.
